## Transport passive scalars with dry mass (`scalar:`) {#sec-ch01-scalar}

### Summary

A passive scalar is a quantity the flow carries without acting on it. snapy stores each scalar as a density and
transports it as a ratio to the dry-air density. The ratio at a face is the reconstructed scalar density over the
reconstructed dry density, and it rides on the dry-mass flux the hydro operator has just computed. This section
follows that call, which runs after the hydro call in every stage.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Form the face ratio $r_{n,f} = \hat\rho_{n,f}/\hat\rho_{\mathrm d,f}$ (@eq-ch01-scalar-face) and upwind it with the hydro dry-mass flux.

**Data.** In: `scalar_s` [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$], `hydro_u` and the hydro fluxes. Out: the scalar stage increment.

**Placement.** After the hydro call in every stage; the parent block combines the result.

**Activation.** `scalar/names` or `scalar/nvar` (default 0); `upper-bound` default $-1$ (off).

**Guarantee / limits.** A uniform ratio stays uniform; the face ratio is fifth order with `cp5` and `weno5` on a smooth column; a face whose reconstructed dry density is not positive takes the donor cell's ratio.

**Evidence.** `test_scalar.release`, `test_scalar_stratified_python` (fitted orders); see Tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\rho_n$[^rg-0d8fe044c8ef] is the density of passive scalar $n$ (`scalar_s`) and $r_n = \rho_n/\rho_{\mathrm{d}}$ its
mixing ratio per unit dry mass (`scalar_r`).

### Derivation

Write $\mathcal W$ (the reconstruction operator, appendix A, notation group 3) for the face reconstruction of the
scalar block, applied to cell averages along one axis, and
$\hat q_f = \mathcal W[q]_f$ for its value at face $f$. The scalar block forms the face ratio from two
reconstructions, one of the scalar density and one of the dry density
({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}, `face_r`):

$$
r_{n,f} = \begin{cases} \mathcal W[\rho_n]_f\,/\,\mathcal W[\rho_{\mathrm d}]_f, & \mathcal W[\rho_{\mathrm d}]_f > 0,\\
\rho_{n,i}/\rho_{\mathrm d,i}, & \text{otherwise, with } i \text{ the cell on that side of } f. \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ch01-scalar-face}

1. *Uniform ratio.* `ScalarImpl::reset` sets `scale = true` on the interpolant it builds, whatever the card says
   ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}}). With `scale`[^rg-21be26a14922] on, the nonlinear weights see the stencil
   values divided by their own magnitude, so the interpolant is homogeneous of degree one: $\mathcal W[c\,q] =
   c\,\mathcal W[q]$ for a constant $c > 0$. A uniform ratio $r_n$ gives $\rho_n = r_n\rho_{\mathrm d}$ cell by cell, so
   $\mathcal W[\rho_n]_f = r_n\,\mathcal W[\rho_{\mathrm d}]_f$ and @eq-ch01-scalar-face returns $r_n$ on every face.
2. *Order.* Each reconstruction of a smooth density is accurate to the order $p$ of the interpolant, so the
   quotient is $r_n(x_f) + O(\Delta x^p)$ wherever $\rho_{\mathrm d}$[^rg-c3e134f8e620] is bounded away from zero. Reconstructing the
   ratio of cell averages, $\overline{\rho_n}/\overline{\rho_{\mathrm d}}$, would not be: that quotient differs from the
   cell average of $r_n$ by $O(\Delta x^2)$ wherever both $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ and $r_n$ vary, which caps the face
   ratio at second order.
3. *Donor fallback.* Where the reconstructed dry density is not positive the quotient is undefined or of the wrong
   sign; the cell ratio of the side the state belongs to replaces it, which is first order there.

The fitted orders are measured by `test_scalar_stratified_python` (Tests).

### Numerical method

`ScalarImpl::forward` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}) requires `hydro_u` and forms the face
ratio of @eq-ch01-scalar-face from the reconstructed scalar and dry densities. In $x_1$ it uses `precon1`, which
`ScalarImpl::reset` builds with the coordinate's per-face $x_1$ rows when `x1_row_faces` returns faces for the
interpolant (a stretched $x_1$, or `weno5`/`cp5` on a spherical-polar or gnomonic $x_1$), and which is the same module
as the lateral `precon` otherwise ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}},
{{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::x1_row_faces >}}). It feeds the face pair to the Riemann solver
together with the hydro's $x_1$ dry-mass flux. The lateral directions form the same face ratio and exchange the
cross-panel face states with interpolation off. They take the hydro's lateral mass fluxes, with the
scalar's own covariance row when the face-flux covariance is on (@sec-ch12-flux-covariance). The donor factor of the
positivity limiter is exchanged raw and passed through the physical boundary functions in the `sync_theta` closure
before the fluxes are scaled (@sec-ch08). The parent block combines the stage and carries the implicit dry transfer
and the dry sources (@sec-ch01-stage). `ScalarOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/scalar/scalar_options.cpp ScalarOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) reads `nvar` (default 0), lets a `names`[^rg-5f6c85feb7ba]
list set the count, reads `upper-bound` (default $-1$), and reads an optional `reconstruct` block. When that block is
absent the block options take the horizontal hydro reconstruction (`MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). Reconstruction, boundary and limiter
choices set the accuracy; no scalar convergence rate is measured here.

@fig-ch01-scalar-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-scalar-flow
#| fig-cap: "Transport passive scalars with dry mass. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: dry density / scalar density; ratio reconstruction; hydro dry flux; panel states / donor copy; scalar increment."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_scalar_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why the ratio, and what it costs.** Two facts of the code and one bound.

1. The scalar is advected as a ratio so that it rides on the hydro's dry-mass flux exactly. The Riemann call for the
   scalar receives the hydro's $x_1$ flux of `IDN` as the mass flux
   ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}). A uniform ratio is thus transported as a uniform ratio
   (Derivation, step 1).
2. The face ratio costs two reconstructions and one division per face instead of one reconstruction of a ratio
   formed per cell, and the donor fallback costs a `where` over the face states.
3. The donor factor is exchanged raw, because the donor of a seam face is the neighbour's edge cell and an
   interpolated ghost is not its factor (@sec-ch11-exchange).

: Implementation anchors for the scalar transport. {#tbl-ch01-scalar-code}

1. Build `precon` with `scale` forced on, and `precon1` with the per-face $x_1$ rows when the coordinate has them:
   `reset` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}}).
2. Reconstruct the scalar and dry densities, form the face ratio, upwind with the dry-mass fluxes: `forward`
   ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).
3. Exchange and bound the donor factor: `sync_theta` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).
4. Read the count, bound and reconstruction: `from_yaml`
   ({{< code src/scalar/scalar_options.cpp ScalarOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}); the inherited reconstruction is
   set in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}.
5. Carry the implicit dry transfer in the parent: `mass_corr`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).

**How to use it.** Name the scalars, or give their count; the bound is off unless set
({{< code src/scalar/scalar_options.cpp ScalarOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}):

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `limiter`[^rg-ee49227d4789], `scalar`[^rg-79187c4eedd7].
```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state: {type: ideal-gas, limiter: true}  # a positive upper-bound needs the limiter
scalar:
  names: [dye, tracer2]   # sets nvar = 2
  upper-bound: 1.0        # default -1: no bound
  reconstruct: {type: plm}  # omitted: the horizontal hydro reconstruction
```

Refused: a key other than `verbose`, `nvar`, `upper-bound`, `names`, `reconstruct` and `riemann-solver`; inside
`reconstruct` anything but `shock`[^rg-e1a0b3afb85c] and `type`, so a card that sets `scalar/reconstruct/scale` is refused as an
unknown key ({{< code src/scalar/scalar_options.cpp ScalarOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}); the scalar interpolant runs
with `scale` on whatever the card says. Also refused: a Riemann solver other than `upwind`, and
`upper-bound: 0` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}}). The face ratio and the $x_1$ flux are these
lines of `ScalarImpl::forward` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
auto rho = other.at("hydro_u")[IDN].unsqueeze(0);
auto face_r = [&](int dim) {
  auto recon = dim == DIM1 ? precon1 : precon;
  auto rf = recon->forward(rho, dim), r = u / rho;  // donor r if rf <= 0
  return torch::where(rf > 0., recon->forward(u, dim) / rf,
                      torch::stack({r.roll(1, dim), r}));
};
if (_flux1.defined()) {
  auto rlr = face_r(DIM1);
  _flux1.set_(
      priemann->forward(rlr[ILT], rlr[IRT], DIM1, pmb->phydro->flux1()[IDN]));
```

`rho` is the conserved dry density, `rf` its face pair, and `face_r` returns the pair of
@eq-ch01-scalar-face: the quotient where `rf` is positive, else the cell ratio `r` of the side the state comes from
(`r.roll(1, dim)` for the left state, `r` for the right). The last call upwinds the pair with the hydro's dry-mass
flux.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_scalar.<b>` | the scalar density is seeded with the right shape and the increment is finite | `allclose` defaults; exact shape | the API contract |
| `test_scalar.<b>` | the ratio stays within its upper bound and the density nonnegative | $10^{-5}$ float32; $10^{-12}$ float64 | test constants |
| `test_scalar_stratified_python` | the face ratio of @eq-ch01-scalar-face is at least order 4.5 with `cp5` and `weno5` on a smooth stratified column ($n_1$[^rg-b2378306863a] 40 to 160), and finite at a 10:1 and a 100:1 density contact | fitted order $\ge4.5$; finite | test bound |
| `test_scalar_flux_covariance_python`, `test_scalar_cov_x1_split_python` | a tracer carried as a scalar equals the same tracer carried as a hydro species; four $x_1$ blocks equal one | $10^{-12}$; $10^{-13}$ relative | round-off |

: Source assertions for the scalar transport. {#tbl-ch01-scalar-tests}

The assertions are {{< code tests/test_scalar.cpp DeviceTest.initialize_and_transport_scalar >}} and
{{< code tests/test_scalar.cpp DeviceTest.scalar_upper_bound_holds_both_sides >}}.

The C++ ctest runs on CPU and, through the shared device list, on CUDA when the build has it. At the pin all four
pass on CPU; `test_scalar_stratified_python` fits orders 4.99 and 5.00 (`cp5`, $n_1$ 40 to 80 and 80 to 160) and
5.09 and 4.99 (`weno5`), and no non-finite face ratio at either contact.[^sca-run68] The CUDA cases were not run. No
report check exists for this section.

    source build at the pin, with `$SITE` the snapy Python package built from the same checkout against that build,
    CPU, double, 1 process; Python 3.11.13, torch 2.10.0, kintera 2.6.6, GCC 11.5.0]. Output line `order cp5, weno5:

    [False, False]`.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The forward routine divides by the conserved dry density; its behaviour for a zero dry-density field is not
established by the cited tests. The upper-bound and positivity mechanisms are documented by @sec-ch10 and
@sec-ch08; combinations remain in @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
